```{r}
# Unit 1-7 packages
library(tidyverse)
library(class)
library(caret)
library(e1071)
library(GGally)
```

# 1. Data Setup

```{r}
# Read in the case study data
df = read.csv("C:/Users/jorge/Downloads/CaseStudy1-data.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)

# Initial structure and dimensions
dim(df)
str(df)

# Checking for missing values
sapply(df, function(x) sum(is.na(x)))

# Remove constant columns (same value for every employee)
df = df %>% select(-EmployeeCount, -Over18, -StandardHours)

# Summary table of attrition counts and percents
attritionSummary = df %>%
  group_by(Attrition) %>%
  summarize(Count = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round((Count / sum(Count)) * 100, 2))

attritionSummary
```

# 2. Significance Tests

Every candidate feature gets a test. Numeric and rating variables get a t-test (Unit 4).
Categorical variables get a chi-square test. If the p-value is below 0.05, the feature
name is added to `sigFeatures`.

```{r}
# Numeric/rating variables (ratings like 1-4 are treated as numeric)
numericVars = c("MonthlyIncome", "JobLevel", "StockOptionLevel", "Age", "TotalWorkingYears",
                "YearsAtCompany", "YearsInCurrentRole", "YearsWithCurrManager",
                "YearsSinceLastPromotion", "NumCompaniesWorked", "JobInvolvement",
                "JobSatisfaction", "EnvironmentSatisfaction", "RelationshipSatisfaction",
                "WorkLifeBalance", "DistanceFromHome", "TrainingTimesLastYear", "Education",
                "PerformanceRating", "PercentSalaryHike", "HourlyRate", "DailyRate", "MonthlyRate")

# Categorical variables
categoricalVars = c("OverTime", "JobRole", "MaritalStatus", "Department",
                    "BusinessTravel", "EducationField", "Gender")

# Empty lists to hold the significant features
sigNumeric = c()
sigCategorical = c()

# Table to hold every test result
testResults = data.frame()

#  t-tests for numeric variables (Using a loop to make it more condensed)
for(v in numericVars)
{
  result = t.test(df[[v]] ~ df$Attrition)
  print(v)
  print(result)

  testResults = rbind(testResults, data.frame(Feature = v, Test = "t-test",
                                              Statistic = round(result$statistic, 3),
                                              PValue = result$p.value))

  if(result$p.value < 0.05)
  {
    sigNumeric = c(sigNumeric, v)
  }
}

#  Chi-square tests for categorical variables 
for(v in categoricalVars)
{
  result = chisq.test(table(df[[v]], df$Attrition))
  print(v)
  print(result)

  testResults = rbind(testResults, data.frame(Feature = v, Test = "Chi-square",
                                              Statistic = round(result$statistic, 3),
                                              PValue = result$p.value))

  if(result$p.value < 0.05)
  {
    sigCategorical = c(sigCategorical, v)
  }
}

# Results 
testResults$Significant = ifelse(testResults$PValue < 0.05, "Yes", "No")
testResults$PValue = signif(testResults$PValue, 3)
rownames(testResults) = NULL

# All tests
testResults %>% arrange(PValue)

# Significant features found by the tests
sigFeatures = c(sigNumeric, sigCategorical)

sigNumeric
sigCategorical
sigFeatures
length(sigFeatures)

# Features that were NOT significant
testResults %>% filter(Significant == "No")
```

# 3. Feature Summaries

What percent left in each group (categorical and rating variables), and the average
and median for leavers vs. stayers (numeric variables).

```{r}
# Variables with a small number of groups: counts and percent who left
groupVars = c("OverTime", "JobRole", "MaritalStatus", "Department", "BusinessTravel",
              "EducationField", "Gender", "JobLevel", "StockOptionLevel", "JobInvolvement",
              "JobSatisfaction", "EnvironmentSatisfaction", "RelationshipSatisfaction",
              "WorkLifeBalance", "Education", "PerformanceRating", "NumCompaniesWorked",
              "TrainingTimesLastYear")

for(v in groupVars)
{
  counts = table(df[[v]], df$Attrition)
  percentLeft = round(prop.table(counts, 1)[, "Yes"] * 100, 1)
  print(v)
  print(cbind(counts, PercentLeft = percentLeft))
}

# Numeric variables: mean and median for stayed (No) vs left (Yes)
continuousVars = c("MonthlyIncome", "Age", "TotalWorkingYears", "YearsAtCompany",
                   "YearsInCurrentRole", "YearsWithCurrManager", "YearsSinceLastPromotion",
                   "DistanceFromHome", "PercentSalaryHike", "HourlyRate", "DailyRate", "MonthlyRate")

for(v in continuousVars)
{
  print(v)
  print(rbind(Mean = round(tapply(df[[v]], df$Attrition, mean), 2),
              Median = tapply(df[[v]], df$Attrition, median)))
}

# Monthly income grouped into ranges 
df$IncomeGroup = cut(df$MonthlyIncome,
                     breaks = c(0, 3000, 6000, 10000, 20000),
                     labels = c("Under $3K", "$3K-$6K", "$6K-$10K", "Over $10K"))

df %>%
  group_by(IncomeGroup, Attrition) %>%
  summarize(Count = n()) %>%
  mutate(Percent = round((Count / sum(Count)) * 100, 2))
```

# 5. Model Data Setup

Both models use the 18 significant features from Section 2.

```{r}
# Copy of the data for modeling
dfModel = df

# KNN needs numbers, so the 5 significant categorical features become 0/1 flags
# (one flag for the highest-risk group found in the EDA)
dfModel$OverTimeNum = ifelse(dfModel$OverTime == "Yes", 1, 0)
dfModel$SingleNum = ifelse(dfModel$MaritalStatus == "Single", 1, 0)
dfModel$SalesRepNum = ifelse(dfModel$JobRole == "Sales Representative", 1, 0)
dfModel$SalesDeptNum = ifelse(dfModel$Department == "Sales", 1, 0)
dfModel$TravelFreqNum = ifelse(dfModel$BusinessTravel == "Travel_Frequently", 1, 0)

# Standardize the 13 significant numeric features 
dfModel$Z_Income = scale(dfModel$MonthlyIncome)
dfModel$Z_JobLevel = scale(dfModel$JobLevel)
dfModel$Z_Stock = scale(dfModel$StockOptionLevel)
dfModel$Z_Age = scale(dfModel$Age)
dfModel$Z_TotalYears = scale(dfModel$TotalWorkingYears)
dfModel$Z_YearsAtCompany = scale(dfModel$YearsAtCompany)
dfModel$Z_YearsInRole = scale(dfModel$YearsInCurrentRole)
dfModel$Z_YearsWithManager = scale(dfModel$YearsWithCurrManager)
dfModel$Z_JobInvolvement = scale(dfModel$JobInvolvement)
dfModel$Z_JobSat = scale(dfModel$JobSatisfaction)
dfModel$Z_EnvSat = scale(dfModel$EnvironmentSatisfaction)
dfModel$Z_WLB = scale(dfModel$WorkLifeBalance)
dfModel$Z_Distance = scale(dfModel$DistanceFromHome)

# KNN features: 5 flags + 13 standardized numeric = 18
knnVars = c("OverTimeNum", "SingleNum", "SalesRepNum", "SalesDeptNum", "TravelFreqNum",
            "Z_Income", "Z_JobLevel", "Z_Stock", "Z_Age", "Z_TotalYears", "Z_YearsAtCompany",
            "Z_YearsInRole", "Z_YearsWithManager", "Z_JobInvolvement", "Z_JobSat",
            "Z_EnvSat", "Z_WLB", "Z_Distance")

# Naive Bayes can use the 18 significant features directly
nbVars = sigFeatures

length(knnVars)
length(nbVars)

# 70/30 train/test split
set.seed(4)
splitPerc = .7
trainIndices = sample(1:dim(dfModel)[1], round(splitPerc * dim(dfModel)[1]))
train = dfModel[trainIndices,]
test = dfModel[-trainIndices,]
```

# 6. KNN (Default Cutoff of 0.5)

```{r}
# Loop over many k 
numks = 30
knnResults = data.frame(k = numeric(numks), Accuracy = numeric(numks),
                        Sensitivity = numeric(numks), Specificity = numeric(numks))

for(i in 1:numks)
{
  classifications = knn(train[,knnVars], test[,knnVars], train$Attrition, prob = TRUE, k = i)
  CM = confusionMatrix(table(classifications, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
  knnResults$k[i] = i
  knnResults$Accuracy[i] = CM$overall[1]
  knnResults$Sensitivity[i] = CM$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  knnResults$Specificity[i] = CM$byClass["Specificity"]
}

knnResults

plot(knnResults$k, knnResults$Accuracy, type = "l", ylim = c(0,1), col = "blue",
     xlab = "k", ylab = "Rate", main = "KNN Performance by k (Cutoff 0.5)")
lines(knnResults$k, knnResults$Sensitivity, col = "red")
lines(knnResults$k, knnResults$Specificity, col = "darkgreen")
legend("right", legend = c("Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"),
       col = c("blue", "red", "darkgreen"), lty = 1)

# Default KNN model with k = 5
classifications = knn(train[,knnVars], test[,knnVars], train$Attrition, prob = TRUE, k = 5)
confusionMatrix(table(classifications, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
```

# 7. Naive Bayes (Default Cutoff of 0.5)

```{r}
# One train/test split (same split as KNN)
model = naiveBayes(train[,nbVars], train$Attrition, laplace = 1)
nbPred = predict(model, test[,nbVars])
confusionMatrix(table(nbPred, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")

# Average over many train/test splits 
iterations = 100
masterAcc = matrix(nrow = iterations)
masterSens = matrix(nrow = iterations)
masterSpec = matrix(nrow = iterations)

for(j in 1:iterations)
{
  trainIndices = sample(1:dim(dfModel)[1], round(splitPerc * dim(dfModel)[1]))
  train = dfModel[trainIndices,]
  test = dfModel[-trainIndices,]

  model = naiveBayes(train[,nbVars], train$Attrition, laplace = 1)
  CM = confusionMatrix(table(predict(model, test[,nbVars]), test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
  masterAcc[j] = CM$overall[1]
  masterSens[j] = CM$byClass["Sensitivity"]
  masterSpec[j] = CM$byClass["Specificity"]
}

colMeans(masterAcc)
colMeans(masterSens)
colMeans(masterSpec)
```

# 8. Tuning for 60% Sensitivity and Specificity
## Naive Bayes: tune the cutoff

```{r}
thresholds = seq(0.05, 0.50, by = 0.05)

nbAccMat = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = length(thresholds))
nbSensMat = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = length(thresholds))
nbSpecMat = matrix(nrow = iterations, ncol = length(thresholds))

set.seed(4)
for(j in 1:iterations)
{
  trainIndices = sample(1:dim(dfModel)[1], round(splitPerc * dim(dfModel)[1]))
  train = dfModel[trainIndices,]
  test = dfModel[-trainIndices,]

  model = naiveBayes(train[,nbVars], train$Attrition, laplace = 1)
  nbProbs = predict(model, test[,nbVars], type = "raw")

  for(i in 1:length(thresholds))
  {
    nbClass = factor(ifelse(nbProbs[,"Yes"] > thresholds[i], "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
    CM = confusionMatrix(table(nbClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
    nbAccMat[j,i] = CM$overall[1]
    nbSensMat[j,i] = CM$byClass["Sensitivity"]
    nbSpecMat[j,i] = CM$byClass["Specificity"]
  }
}

nbTune = data.frame(Threshold = thresholds,
                    Accuracy = colMeans(nbAccMat),
                    Sensitivity = colMeans(nbSensMat),
                    Specificity = colMeans(nbSpecMat))
nbTune$Lower = pmin(nbTune$Sensitivity, nbTune$Specificity)

round(nbTune, 3)

# Best cutoff
bestNB = nbTune[which.max(nbTune$Lower),]
bestNB

plot(nbTune$Threshold, nbTune$Sensitivity, type = "l", ylim = c(0,1), col = "red",
     xlab = "Cutoff for 'Yes'", ylab = "Rate", main = "Naive Bayes: Sensitivity and Specificity by Cutoff")
lines(nbTune$Threshold, nbTune$Specificity, col = "darkgreen")
abline(h = 0.6, lty = 2)
legend("right", legend = c("Sensitivity", "Specificity", "60% target"),
       col = c("red", "darkgreen", "black"), lty = c(1, 1, 2))
```

## KNN: tune k and the cutoff

```{r}
ks = seq(3, 25, by = 2)
knnIterations = 50
knnTune = data.frame()

set.seed(4)
for(m in 1:length(ks))
{
  accMat = matrix(nrow = knnIterations, ncol = length(thresholds))
  sensMat = matrix(nrow = knnIterations, ncol = length(thresholds))
  specMat = matrix(nrow = knnIterations, ncol = length(thresholds))

  for(j in 1:knnIterations)
  {
    trainIndices = sample(1:dim(dfModel)[1], round(splitPerc * dim(dfModel)[1]))
    train = dfModel[trainIndices,]
    test = dfModel[-trainIndices,]

    classifications = knn(train[,knnVars], test[,knnVars], train$Attrition, prob = TRUE, k = ks[m])
    probs = attr(classifications, "prob")
    probYes = ifelse(classifications == "Yes", probs, 1 - probs)

    for(i in 1:length(thresholds))
    {
      newClass = factor(ifelse(probYes > thresholds[i], "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
      CM = confusionMatrix(table(newClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
      accMat[j,i] = CM$overall[1]
      sensMat[j,i] = CM$byClass["Sensitivity"]
      specMat[j,i] = CM$byClass["Specificity"]
    }
  }

  knnTune = rbind(knnTune, data.frame(k = ks[m], Threshold = thresholds,
                                      Accuracy = colMeans(accMat),
                                      Sensitivity = colMeans(sensMat),
                                      Specificity = colMeans(specMat)))
}

knnTune$Lower = pmin(knnTune$Sensitivity, knnTune$Specificity)

# Settings where both sensitivity and specificity are at least 60%
knnTune %>% filter(Sensitivity >= 0.6, Specificity >= 0.6) %>% arrange(desc(Lower))

# Best k and cutoff
bestKNN = knnTune[which.max(knnTune$Lower),]
bestKNN
```

## Tuned models on the original split

```{r}
# Same split as Sections 6 and 7
set.seed(4)
trainIndices = sample(1:dim(dfModel)[1], round(splitPerc * dim(dfModel)[1]))
train = dfModel[trainIndices,]
test = dfModel[-trainIndices,]

# Tuned KNN
classifications = knn(train[,knnVars], test[,knnVars], train$Attrition, prob = TRUE, k = bestKNN$k)
probs = attr(classifications, "prob")
probYes = ifelse(classifications == "Yes", probs, 1 - probs)
knnTunedClass = factor(ifelse(probYes > bestKNN$Threshold, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
confusionMatrix(table(knnTunedClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")

# Tuned Naive Bayes
model = naiveBayes(train[,nbVars], train$Attrition, laplace = 1)
nbProbs = predict(model, test[,nbVars], type = "raw")
nbTunedClass = factor(ifelse(nbProbs[,"Yes"] > bestNB$Threshold, "Yes", "No"), levels = c("No", "Yes"))
confusionMatrix(table(nbTunedClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes")
```

# 9. Model Comparison

```{r}
# Default settings (cutoff 0.5) pulled from the tuning tables
knnDefault = knnTune[knnTune$k == 5 & abs(knnTune$Threshold - 0.5) < 0.001,]
nbDefault = nbTune[abs(nbTune$Threshold - 0.5) < 0.001,]

modelResults = data.frame(
  Model = rep(c("KNN (k=5, cutoff 0.5)", "KNN (tuned)", "NB (cutoff 0.5)", "NB (tuned)"), each = 3),
  Metric = rep(c("Accuracy", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"), 4),
  Value = c(knnDefault$Accuracy, knnDefault$Sensitivity, knnDefault$Specificity,
            bestKNN$Accuracy, bestKNN$Sensitivity, bestKNN$Specificity,
            nbDefault$Accuracy, nbDefault$Sensitivity, nbDefault$Specificity,
            bestNB$Accuracy, bestNB$Sensitivity, bestNB$Specificity) * 100
)

modelResults$Model = factor(modelResults$Model,
                            levels = c("KNN (k=5, cutoff 0.5)", "KNN (tuned)", "NB (cutoff 0.5)", "NB (tuned)"))

modelResults

# Grouped bar chart (Unit 2 position = "dodge")
modelResults %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Metric, y = Value, fill = Model)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 1)), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), vjust = -0.3, size = 3) +
  ggtitle("Average Test-Set Performance by Model") +
  xlab("Metric") + ylab("Percent (%)")

# F1 score for the tuned models on the original split (precision and recall combined)
cmKnnTuned = confusionMatrix(table(knnTunedClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes", mode = "everything")
cmNBTuned = confusionMatrix(table(nbTunedClass, test$Attrition), positive = "Yes", mode = "everything")
cmKnnTuned$byClass["F1"]
```

# 10. Cost / Savings Analysis

```{r}
annualSalary = test$MonthlyIncome * 12
leftYes = test$Attrition == "Yes"

# every leaver has to be replaced
noModelLow = sum(annualSalary[leftYes]) * 0.5
noModelHigh = sum(annualSalary[leftYes]) * 4

costResults = data.frame()

for(m in c("KNN (tuned)", "NB (tuned)"))
{
  if(m == "KNN (tuned)") { pred = knnTunedClass } else { pred = nbTunedClass }

  flagged = sum(pred == "Yes")
  caught = pred == "Yes" & leftYes
  incentiveCost = flagged * 200

  costResults = rbind(costResults, data.frame(
    Model = m,
    Flagged = flagged,
    LeaversCaught = sum(caught),
    LeaversMissed = sum(pred == "No" & leftYes),
    IncentiveCost = incentiveCost,
    SavingsLow = sum(annualSalary[caught]) * 0.5 - incentiveCost,
    SavingsHigh = sum(annualSalary[caught]) * 4 - incentiveCost,
    # share of caught leavers the incentive must keep to pay for itself 
    BreakEvenPercent = round(incentiveCost / (sum(annualSalary[caught]) * 0.5) * 100, 1)))
}

noModelLow
noModelHigh
costResults
```

# 11. Competition Set Predictions

The final model is Naive Bayes with the 18 significant features and the tuned cutoff.
For the predictions it is trained on all 870 employees.

```{r}
comp = read.csv("C:/Users/jorge/Downloads/CaseStudy1CompSet No Attrition.csv", header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = TRUE)
dim(comp)

# Final model trained on all 870 employees
finalModel = naiveBayes(dfModel[,nbVars], dfModel$Attrition, laplace = 1)

# Probability of leaving, then the tuned cutoff
compProbs = predict(finalModel, comp[,nbVars], type = "raw")
comp$Attrition = ifelse(compProbs[,"Yes"] > bestNB$Threshold, "Yes", "No")

# Kept ID and prediction and ordered by ID 
predictions = comp %>% select(ID, Attrition) %>% arrange(ID)
table(predictions$Attrition)

write.csv(predictions, "C:/Users/jorge/Downloads/Case1PredictionsVazquez Attrition.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
